Container.Name: goatmediastackarr
Container.Overview: [b]GoatMediaStackarr: a whole media stack in one container[/b][br]Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Prowlarr, Bazarr, qBittorrent, SABnzbd, Jellyfin and Seerr, plus optional Tautulli, Plex and FlareSolverr. They're all connected to each other on first start, behind one interface and one login. A built-in VPN (WireGuard or OpenVPN) with a kill switch covers the download apps only. Runs on x86 and 64-bit ARM. Web page on port 2806.[br][br][b]Before you install: storage[/b][br]- Image: about 2.4 GB on x86 and 2.2 GB on ARM. Make sure your Docker image file has room.[br]- App data grows over time. Jellyfin's (and Plex's) artwork, thumbnails and databases can reach many GB in a big library. Keep App data on your cache or another SSD, not the array. Jellyfin won't start with less than 2 GB free there.[br]- Separate Media and Downloads folders (the default) means finished downloads are copied into your library. A torrent that keeps seeding takes up its space twice until you remove it. To avoid this, map one shared folder and set "Media folder in container" and "Downloads folder in container" inside it; then files are hardlinked instead of copied.[br][br][b]Before you install: data loss[/b][br]- App data holds every app's settings and database in one folder. Deleting it, or a broken disk, wipes all of them at once. Back it up, for example with the Appdata Backup plugin. Removing or reinstalling the container is safe; deleting the folder is not.[br]- Sonarr, Radarr and Lidarr manage your media folder. They rename and move files, replace files with better copies when they upgrade (the old file is deleted unless you set a recycle bin in their settings), and delete files from disk if you choose "delete files" when removing a show, movie or artist.[br]- Don't run this alongside your existing Sonarr, Radarr or qBittorrent on the same media folder. Both setups will download, rename and upgrade the same files. Bring your setup in from the Stack page, then stop the old containers.[br]- Importing replaces settings with the same name. Bringing in your existing setup copies its quality profiles, custom formats, delay and release profiles and file naming, and replaces any with the same name in the built-in apps. Your old apps are only read from, and media files are never moved or copied.[br]- latest is rebuilt every Monday with the newest version of each app. App updates can upgrade their databases in ways an older version can't read, so going back to an older image may not work. Back up App data before updating. For fewer surprises, use a version tag like :0.3.0 instead of latest.[br]- This is early software (version 0.x). Test it before trusting it with a library you can't replace.[br][br][b]VPN and network[/b][br]- The container needs NET_ADMIN and /dev/net/tun for the VPN; these are already in the template. It does not run privileged.[br]- With the VPN on, the download apps stay offline until a working VPN file is in App data/vpn. That's the kill switch at work, not a fault.[br]- With the VPN off, torrent and usenet traffic uses your own internet connection.[br]- Ports 2806, 8096 (Jellyfin) and 5055 (Seerr) each have their own login. Don't open them to the internet without a reverse proxy or a VPN of your own.[br][br][b]Good to know[/b][br]- Plex isn't included in the image. When you turn it on, it's downloaded from plex.tv on first start, and it's proprietary software under Plex's own terms.[br]- FlareSolverr is x86 only. When turned on, it downloads itself (with a browser) on first start.[br]- Files are written as PUID/PGID (99:100 on Unraid). Existing files in your media folder are never re-owned.
Container.Requires: NET_ADMIN and /dev/net/tun for the built-in VPN (already set in Extra Parameters). App data on a cache or SSD pool, with room to grow. Back up App data before updating.

Config.Name: Web port
Config.Description: GoatMediaStackarr web page

Config.Name: Jellyfin port
Config.Description: For Jellyfin apps on TVs and phones

Config.Name: Seerr port
Config.Description: Seerr's own request page, for family and friends to ask for shows and movies

Config.Name: Plex port
Config.Description: Only used if Plex is turned on (add plex to Apps to run)

Config.Name: Plex claim code
Config.Description: Only for built-in Plex: a code from https://plex.tv/claim links it to your Plex account. Codes last 4 minutes, so start the container right after. Not needed again once linked.

Config.Name: Your Plex address
Config.Description: Only if Plex runs outside this container and you have not added it under Settings, then Apps: like http://192.168.1.10:32400. Seerr signs in through it.

Config.Name: Your Plex token
Config.Description: The X-Plex-Token for the Plex address above

Config.Name: Seerr media server
Config.Description: Which media server Seerr uses when both Jellyfin and Plex run

Config.Name: Update Plex
Config.Description: Built-in Plex: get the newest public Plex at each start

Config.Name: Torrent port
Config.Description: Incoming torrent connections when the VPN is off. Not used with the VPN on.

Config.Name: Torrent port (UDP)
Config.Description: Same as above, UDP

Config.Name: App data
Config.Description: Settings and databases of every app, plus the vpn folder for your VPN file. Back this up.

Config.Name: Media
Config.Description: Your library: tv, movies and music folders are made inside it

Config.Name: Downloads
Config.Description: Torrent and usenet downloads

Config.Name: Media folder in container
Config.Description: Change only if you map one shared folder for both (for example /data/media), so downloads can be hardlinked instead of copied

Config.Name: Downloads folder in container
Config.Description: Change only if you map one shared folder for both (for example /data/downloads)

Config.Name: VPN on
Config.Description: true sends the download apps through your VPN with a kill switch

Config.Name: VPN type
Config.Description: wireguard: put the provider's .conf in App data/vpn. openvpn: put the .ovpn there.

Config.Name: VPN username
Config.Description: OpenVPN only, if your provider needs it

Config.Name: VPN password
Config.Description: OpenVPN only

Config.Name: Apps through VPN
Config.Description: Which apps use the VPN

Config.Name: VPN port forwarding
Config.Description: natpmp for ProtonVPN and other NAT-PMP providers: opens a port and gives it to qBittorrent

Config.Name: Port forwarding gateway
Config.Description: NAT-PMP gateway inside the tunnel (10.2.0.1 for ProtonVPN)

Config.Name: Apps to run
Config.Description: Remove any you do not want. Add plex for a built-in Plex server, tautulli for Plex statistics, and flaresolverr to get past Cloudflare checks on indexer sites (x86 only).

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User that owns files (99 is nobody on Unraid)

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group that owns files (100 is users on Unraid)

Config.Name: Time zone
Config.Description: For schedules and logs

Config.Name: Graphics card
Config.Description: Optional: /dev/dri for Intel/AMD hardware transcoding in Jellyfin
